You can invest your Roth account in almost any stock or fund.
   Roth is a word used to explain the tax structure.   So if you invest in a growth stock or fund, the growth is tax free. If you invest in cash the growth is tax free.
  I have put $50,000 in a Roth 401k over the last 12 years. I invested it in the same funds as my pre-tax money. I paid taxes on the 50,000 as it went in. My balance in that Roth account is $148,000. When I pull that money out I owe no taxes on any of it.
If you’re investing for growth, buy DGRO.  If you’re investing for cash, buy something else.
